BATCH E · BOARD 3 OF 6

Domain viewers and the visualisation builder

Screens 9–10. Five viewers, one per data shape. Each is a reading tool with a shared spine — visibility chip, provenance line, an annotation the discussion thread can anchor to, and a stated limit on what it will not do. None of them is an analysis environment: that is what the reproducible launch on board E5 is for.

COORDINATE PRECISION
Rounded to 100 m for the public copy. Exact coordinates are controlled-access — protected species sites are re-identifiable from a map.
Will not: interpolate a surface between points. A rendered kriging map that nobody parameterised is a picture, not a result.

WHAT ALL FIVE VIEWERS SHARE
01The same chrome: visibility chip, format and provenance line, and the same control row position. Learning one teaches you all five.
02Every viewer accepts an anchored annotation — an x/y/z coordinate, a ppm value, a base range, a map polygon, a time window — so the adjacent discussion can point at something precise.
03Each states a will not. A viewer that quietly segments, aligns, interpolates or kriges produces numbers with no recorded method, which is the opposite of what this platform is for.
04Nothing a viewer computes is written back to the dataset. Your integrals and selections are yours; the deposited bytes do not move.
WHY NOT ONE UNIVERSAL VIEWER
Because the five shapes disagree about what an axis is. A generic table-and-chart viewer would render a z-stack as 18 rows and an NMR spectrum as 32,768 numbers — technically correct and useless at the bench. Five viewers is more surface to maintain and the right trade.

A CHART IS AN ARTIFACT
Saving it records the dataset version, the encoding and the filters as a spec — not a PNG. Open the chart in six months and it either renders identically or tells you the underlying version moved.
"copy as code" gives you the equivalent ggplot or matplotlib — the builder is a starting point, not a ceiling
